items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: when I was with Woody Herman’s band, we had a baseball team

ctx.x: Did you get to rub elbows much with Joe Williams?

One of my real — I knew Joe Williams before the Basie band, because when I was with Woody Herman’s band, we had a baseball team. You know we had a team. And we used to play. Joe was with Red Saunders in Chicago and we used to play them in baseball.

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: until I got with Woody Herman’s band really.

ctx.x: Everybody in the world has one. So, and you could relate to all, and all kids who play in the streets could relate to my stories, you know. So and I was lucky to have a great childhood. I grew up with Tiny Kahn, see Tiny Kahn is when I was from 6 years old until I went in the Army at 19 or 18, until I got with Woody Herman’s band really. We were together day and night. And if you can, people who know these names can imagine what we looked like at 15 years old, we looked like Peter Lorre and Sydney Greenstreet…

items.q: He joined the band in Milwaukee.

ctx.x: Yeah, he came -- he had been with Tommy
Dorsey for a short time. And I heard about him -- he had been suggested and I heard about him, and brought him in. He joined the band in Milwaukee. I think we were doing theaters.
This band was much more hard pop oriented, it seems to me.
